- If sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.50), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent prices are trending up.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth out forecast peaks and troughs by 1–2 days to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.50), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 5–10 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3%.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in first 3–5 days, model is likely underestimating momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.75 to -0.50), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift within 2–3 days.
